text.p: COPENHAGEN, Sept 18 (Reuter) Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Danish sales of most French wines have increased again after last summer's consumer ban in protest of the French nuclear tests in the Pacific Ocean. Only Bordeaux wines have had no comeback yet, as retailers had given over shelf space to comparable Spanish, Italian and South African wines.
--- Copenhagen airport management acknowledges that the airport has too many late flights, with 40 percent delays in April, May and June this year, mainly Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) flights.
--- Environment minister Svend Auken is to sign a contract this week in Cape Town, South Africa, granting 12 million crowns to the first chemical cleaning plant in the country.
--- Dairy group MD Foods and dairy firm Kloever Maelk are planning a common cheese plant which is to produce close to 30,000 tonnes a year.

--- Businesses are to invest millions of crowns in securing themselves with for example new alarms and TV monitors in years to come, the security business says. Danish companies spend 1.7 billion crowns on securing themselves each year which is the lowest security spending in Europe.

--- The contracting firms C.G. Jensen A/S and H. Hoffmann & Soenner A/S are to build a new Scandinavian Airlines System freight terminal at Copenhagen Airport worth 200 million crowns. The terminal is to be ready in the beginning of 1997.
